analysis.evidence: The address אֲדֹנָי יַהְוֶה and the first-person question בַּמָּה אֵדַע (“how will I know?”) are the words Abram speaks.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ is prefixed to a third-person masculine singular Qal wayyiqtol verb.

analysis.evidence: Abram addresses Yahweh by name immediately after אֲדֹנָי and asks how he will know that he will inherit the land. The qamats in אֲדֹנָי distinguishes the divine title from אֲדֹנִי, the ordinary singular form meaning “my lord.”
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct noun with a first-person singular possessive suffix, used as a singular divine title in direct address.
analysis.sense: אֲדֹנָי as a title for God

analysis.evidence: Abram addresses his question to אֲדֹנָי יַהְוֶה, “Lord Yahweh.” The marked word names the one he addresses.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun in direct address, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: Abram asks בַּמָּה אֵדַע, “By what means shall I know?” The כִּי clause gives the content of that knowledge, “that I shall inherit it.”
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, first person common singular. The initial א marks the first-person subject.
analysis.sense: to know that something is the case

analysis.evidence: בַּמָּה אֵדַע asks “How shall I know?” The clause כִּי אִירָשֶׁנָּה supplies what Abram wants to know, “that I shall inherit it.”
analysis.morphology: Unprefixed Hebrew conjunction with no suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: Abram asks how he will know that he will inherit the land. The feminine singular suffix refers to הָאָרֶץ, the land promised to him in the preceding verse.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, first person common singular, with a third-person feminine singular direct-object suffix.
